name: Yentl Collin
intro: I work on generative models at the Institute of Foundation Models (MBZUAI), with the Speech / LLM team. My interests lie in flow matching, discrete diffusion, and efficient generation for speech and language.

I am a student in the MVA master’s program at ENS Paris-Saclay and at École des Ponts et Chaussées. Previously, I worked on interpretable time-series models in Chirag J. Patel’s lab at Harvard University.

interests.title: Generative modeling
interests.text: Flow matching, flow-map distillation, and discrete diffusion for speech, language, and images.

interests.title: Efficient foundation models
interests.text: Few-step inference, inference-time scaling, and distillation from Transformers to state-space models.

interests.title: Time series & healthcare
interests.text: Interpretable state-space models, forecasting, and personalized glucose management.

publications.title: Distill Locally, Schedule Globally: Flow Maps for Few-Step Text-to-Speech
publications.description: Flow-map distillation of large-scale flow-matching text-to-speech models for few-step inference.
publications.authors: Yentl Collin, Evan Dufraisse, Amr Mohamed, Amine Khelif Khelif, Dani Bouch, Guokan Shang

publications.title: SSM-CGM: Interpretable State-Space Forecasting Model of Continuous Glucose Monitoring for Personalized Diabetes Management
publications.description: Interpretable state-space modeling for continuous glucose forecasting and personalized diabetes management.
publications.authors: Shakson Isaac*, Yentl Collin*, Chirag J. Patel

outside: Outside research, I enjoy playing the cello, which I studied for fourteen years at the Conservatoire de Toulouse, as well as football and swimming.
